narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: After the harvest has been stripped, Manawydan catches the slowest mouse and keeps it in his glove. His questioning reveals that it is part of a deliberate enchantment, not an ordinary pest.

narrativeBlocks.title: The mouse is not an ordinary thief
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (Guest translation; whitespace normalized): “he caught it and put it in his glove, and tied up the opening of the glove with a string, and kept it with him, and returned to the palace. Then he came to the hall where Kicva was, and he lighted a fire, and hung the glove by the string upon a peg. “What hast thou there, lord?” said Kicva. “A thief,” said he, “”

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: The tale delays the explanation. Manawydan observes what happened, preserves the evidence, and questions the mouse rather than answering magical trouble with immediate violence.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read it carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: The story explains Llwyd's act as revenge for an earlier episode in Pwyll's tale. Keep that narrative connection explicit; do not make it a generic claim about all Welsh enchantment stories.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: Follow the evidence from the ruined harvest to the captured mouse, then to Llwyd's account of the revenge behind the spell.
